text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days, driver-level randomization leaks, no MDE/power","detail":"The test runs only 5 days, below the 14-day minimum. Randomizing by driver leaks between arms because dispatch is a shared marketplace: drivers compete for the same orders, so one arm's assignments affect the other's. No MDE or power analysis is stated.","evidence_quote":"A/B test randomized by driver. Run for 5 days.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at a unit that limits interference (e.g., geo or time-slice switchback), run at least 14 days, and document MDE and power calculations."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Rating-based tie-break affects driver offers/earnings with no recorded review","detail":"Changing dispatch to use driver rating as a tie-break alters which drivers receive offers, and therefore their earning opportunities. This is a pay-adjacent, policy-controlled area, and no policy or fairness review is recorded; the Reviews section lists only engineering capacity.","evidence_quote":"Dispatch engineering has capacity next sprint.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record the required pay/policy (and fairness) review for the dispatch change, including the impact of rating-based tie-breaks on driver earnings, before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No driver-side or delivery-time guardrails for dispatch change","detail":"A dispatch change that favors nearby drivers can concentrate offers among some drivers and hurt others, and can alter offer acceptance and delivery times. Guardrails cover defects and safety only; driver earnings/offer distribution, offer acceptance or decline rate, and delivery time or ETA accuracy are absent.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for driver earnings or offer distribution equity, offer acceptance rate, and delivery time/ETA accuracy, with stop thresholds."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Problem claim lacks quantification and sourcing; baseline unsourced","detail":"The problem says offers 'sometimes' go to farther drivers, citing an audit report without a figure. The 87% on-time baseline has no source or measurement window, and there is no evidence that proximity drives on-time performance.","evidence_quote":"baseline 87%, target 89% within 6 weeks","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the source and period for the 87% baseline and quantify how often suboptimal assignments occur and their impact on on-time rate."}]}
